newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel closes Hebron shops, sparking clashes.
newsitem.headline: Israel closes Hebron shops, sparking clashes.

text.p: Israel shut down Palestinian shops in parts of the West Bank city of Hebron on Thursday, sparking clashes between angry Palestinian youths and Israeli soldiers, witnesses said.

The army closed the shops in response to shots that were fired overnight at a building housing Jewish settlers. Army jeeps patrolled the portion of the city under Israeli control to enforce the shutdown.
Witnesses said soldiers fired rubber bullets at youths who pelted them with stones and hurled fire bombs across the line that divides the city in two. There were no immediate reports of injuries.

Major-General Uzi Dayan, the Israeli army commander over the central region that includes the West Bank, ordered the shops closed and instructed troops to keep roadblocks, erected last week around Hebron, in place indefinitely, the army said.
Dayan also ordered soldiers to be stationed along the dividing line between Israeli and Palestinian areas.
Witnesses and Israeli military sources said no one was hurt when the shots were fired late on Wednesday but at least one bullet hit an outer wall of the Jewish settler enclave of Beit Hadassah.
Israel controls 20 percent of the city under a peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO). In January, Israel handed over the remaining 80 percent to Palestinian self-rule.

A Jewish woman faces up to 26 years in prison for putting up posters in Hebron last month portraying the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig. The posters sparked a wave of unrest in the city where 400 Jews live amid 100,000 Arabs.
